authority.relay_persistence: devices and links only; no command or result bodies; binding key plaintext never persisted
authority.mac_binding_key_store: Keychain userPresence for plaintext; SHA-256 digest in remote-control.json
authority.ws_auth: after Upgrade, first text frame { op: auth, token }; handshake URL must not carry token

invariants: One association binds one Android remote to one Mac. One Android may hold many associations, and one Mac may be linked from many Androids.
Mac must have a binding key before starting association. create_pairing requires a non-empty binding_key_digest; the digest is held only on the in-memory pairing until redeem or expiry.
redeem requires binding_key and succeeds only when SHA-256(binding_key) matches the pairing digest via constant-time comparison. Failed verification must not create a link.
Changing the Mac binding key does not revoke existing links; it only affects subsequent pairings.
The relay forwards only the fixed action whitelist in memory and returns mac_offline immediately when that Mac socket is absent.
accepted means the peer socket received the frame. result is the Mac execution outcome and is correlated by request_id.
Deleting an association removes the route immediately and notifies the peer that is still connected.
The remote channel cannot run shell, free text, root changes, model switching, quit, WeChat send, or key/text injection.

WebSocket clients connect to /v1/ws without a token query. Identity is established only by the first text frame { op: auth, token } after Upgrade; device_token and link_token remain Bearer secrets. Auth must complete within 5 seconds; frames before auth are rejected.
prohibited_results: Persisting a command, parameter, or result body in the relay route file.
Persisting binding key plaintext or digest on devices/links durable storage.
Routing a command to a Mac that is not the association target.
Reusing a pairing code or accepting an expired code.
Creating a link when binding_key is missing or does not match the pairing digest.
Carrying a role, prompt, binding key, or other credential inside the pairing QR.
Placing device_token or link_token in the WebSocket handshake URL or query string after cutover.
Forwarding app or remote frames before successful ws auth.
